title: We Removed the Last Dark Cloud Over Rings Network
author: Ryan Kung
summary: When a user is behind a Symmetric NAT or mobile carrier firewall where direct P2P hole-punching cannot succeed, Rings bridges stateless cryptographic TURN allocations across multi-hop onion::udp circuits—preserving Tor-grade endpoint separation with zero DID exposure.

title: From Onion Routing to Onion OP: The Evolution of Privacy in Rings
author: Ryan Kung
summary: How Rings expands privacy from hiding who is communicating with whom to distributing multi-step operations across mutually untrusted ring participants with Onion OP.

title: One Lookup, Many Fingers
author: Ryan Kung
summary: Fixing Chord finger maintenance for a ring made of browsers, proving whole runs of finger slots from a single lookup, and the bugs that hid behind a cooperative test harness.

title: Correctness: How We Build Distributed Systems Correct
author: Ryan Kung
summary: Moving correctness for distributed systems and cryptography into explicit mathematical structures: algebraic curve laws, CRDT join-semilattices, and pure state-effect transitions.

title: The Only Way to Save the Internet
author: Ryan Kung
summary: Tackling the Waist of the Internet by connecting web browsers directly over WebRTC, WebAssembly, Chord DHT routing, and multi-chain DIDs.

title: Annual Update from Rings Network
author: Ryan Kung
summary: The first annual progress report submitted to the Cryptography mailing list: Strong Rings DHT, WASM & FFI clients, DID TCP proxy, delegated sessions, and browser extension.
